note: Browser-demo data for the Waits panel. Reports and pressure come from scans of the demo databases, samples from 30-second runs under a small read load; the staging connection's resource samples are synthetic, to show the tier-limit chart.

categories.detail: A read from order_items accounts for 57% of it.
categories.label: In-memory contention
categories.meaning: Short waits on the server's own memory structures (page latches, mutexes). Hot spots such as an ever-increasing key or busy temporary space cause most of it.

queries.text: SELECT [id], [total] FROM [shop].[orders] WHERE [shipped_at] >= DATEADD(day, @P1, '2026-01-01') AND [shipped_at] < DATEADD(day, @P2, '2026-01-01')

categories.detail: A read from order_items accounts for 48% of it. Check its plan for a large scan an index would avoid.
categories.label: Parallel queries
categories.meaning: Threads of a parallel query waiting for each other. Often a big scan that an index would avoid, or work split unevenly across threads.

queries.text: SELECT [id], [total] FROM [shop].[orders] WHERE [shipped_at] >= DATEADD(day, @P1, '2026-01-01') AND [shipped_at] < DATEADD(day, @P2, '2026-01-01')

categories.detail: A read from order_items accounts for 27% of it.
categories.label: Memory grants
categories.meaning: Queries waiting for memory to sort or hash. A few queries that reserve far more than they use can make everyone else queue.

categories.detail: A read from orders accounts for 8% of it.
categories.label: CPU
categories.meaning: Running on a processor, or queued for one. When CPU dominates, queries usually do more work than they need to: scans, conversions, functions evaluated on every row.

queries.text: SELECT [id], [total] FROM [shop].[orders] WHERE [shipped_at] >= DATEADD(day, @P1, '2026-01-01') AND [shipped_at] < DATEADD(day, @P2, '2026-01-01')

categories.attribution: Query Store didn't record this wait for individual queries in the window.
categories.label: Locks
categories.meaning: Waiting for another transaction to release a row or table lock. Long transactions, and missing indexes on the columns updates filter by, make it worse.

categories.attribution: PostgreSQL doesn't time this per statement. Right now samples what sessions wait on.
categories.label: Everything else
categories.meaning: Statement time PostgreSQL doesn't break down: running on CPU, or waiting on locks and events it doesn't time per statement.

categories.detail: A read from orders accounts for 56% of it, reading 16K pages from disk per run.
categories.label: Disk reads
categories.meaning: Waiting for data to come from disk because it wasn't in memory. Usually scans of large tables, or memory too small for the data the workload keeps touching.

queries.text: SELECT id, status, total, created_at FROM orders WHERE customer_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT $2
SELECT id, note FROM orders WHERE created_at > now() - interval $1 ORDER BY note
SELECT count(*), sum(quantity * price) FROM order_items WHERE product_id = $1
SELECT kind, count(*) FROM events WHERE customer_id = $1 GROUP BY kind
SELECT status, count(*), sum(total) FROM orders WHERE created_at > now() - interval $1 GROUP BY status

notes: PostgreSQL keeps no history of what sessions waited on. These totals come from per-statement timing; use Right now to sample what sessions wait on at this moment.

categories.attribution: MySQL doesn't attribute this wait to statements; it is a server-wide total.
categories.label: Row access
categories.meaning: Time inside InnoDB fetching and changing rows. MySQL's table I/O instrument counts rows served from memory too, so this is storage-engine work, not only disk.

categories.attribution: MySQL doesn't attribute this wait to statements; it is a server-wide total.
categories.label: Disk reads
categories.meaning: Waiting for data to come from disk because it wasn't in memory. Usually scans of large tables, or memory too small for the data the workload keeps touching.

categories.attribution: MySQL doesn't attribute this wait to statements; it is a server-wide total.
categories.label: Log writes
categories.meaning: Commits waiting for InnoDB's redo log to reach disk. Many tiny transactions, or slow log storage.
